correctness.rationale: Line-graph neighbor degree identity deg_L(uv)=deg_H(u)+deg_H(v)-2 proves every component is K2, P3 or isolated, for all n>=3. Counterextensions for c>=2 or c=1,b>0 and obstruction to every edge extension for c=0 or c=1,b=0 prove maximality bidirectionally. Labeled component partitions yield exact coefficient factors 2^a a!2^b b!c! and spectrum follows by parity of a. Independent finite direct-adjacency Python check passed 2,131,016 subsets n=3..7; not used as infinite proof.

evidence: Tu, Li and Du (arXiv:2103.01402, 2021), Theorems 1.1/1.2 and 5.1/5.2, give tight universal extremal upper bounds, not exact polynomials of J(n,2).
Duginov et al. (2022) prove general complexity results and give bounds/algorithms.
Tu et al. (2023), Theorem 1.1, bounds the dissociation occupancy fraction of cubic graphs and equality at unions of K4.
Orlovich et al. (2011), conclusion, treat maximum dissociation number for certain line graph classes.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A general algorithm for an extremum is not the exact distribution of all inclusion-maximal sets or the polynomial of all sets. Cubic coverage does not apply: T_n is (2n-4)-regular, never 3-regular for integer n.

evidence: Published work studies maximal dissociating sets, cubic graph bounds, and line graph complexity.
Current formula jointly classifies K2/P3 component partitions, characterizes maximality by c=0 or c=1,b=0, and counts each size.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Prior extremal algorithmic coverage could give the maximum size but does not logically imply the entire polynomial, the minimal maximal cardinality, or each labeled multiplicity. These require the explicit component/maximality bijection proved here.

evidence: T_n=J(n,2)=L(K_n): vertex subsets correspond to edge families in K_n.
For each edge family selected-degree bound on the line graph is equivalent to base components K2 or P3.

The 2011 work discusses line graph maximum-size algorithms, but no inspected exact all-set or maximal-coefficient statement equivalent to this one.

originality.rationale: Exact statement-implication comparison: the 2021 general/maximal-count bound and the 2022 paper addresses general structural bounds and complexity, the 2023 paper a cubic-graph extremal polynomial bound, and the 2011 paper complexity and maximum-size methods for line graphs; none of the inspected mathematical statements gives both J(n,2) coefficient formulas and its maximal family profile. Residual indexing/full-text risks remain.
residual_risks: The full 2011 publisher text was not accessed; its indexed conclusion is relevant to maximum dissociation but not a known exact polynomial.
The complete 2022 Russian-language article was not professionally translated; inspected theorem statements and English abstract concern general complexity and tree algorithms.
Unindexed or differently termed exact triangular-graph enumeration may exist; lack of a retrieved hit cannot certify global novelty.

value.rationale: For the natural high-symmetry Johnson/triangular graph family, the theorem classifies every induced maximum-degree-one set and every inclusion-maximal such set. It determines two natural polynomials and exact full distribution by cardinality, and identifies sharp minimal/maximal sizes with a no-gap spectrum. The structural K2/P3 partition and maximality condition, rather than just numerical computation, make the result useful for degree-bounded induced-subgraph enumeration and 3-path vertex-cover complements.
